syllabusTopics: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection
Anti-derivatives: integration using basic integrals, integration by substitution and by parts methods
The definite integral; the definite integral as an area under the given curve; area between two curves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Area under a curve begins with the ledger/map distinction: the definite integral is signed (net displacement), the geometric area is |f| split at the roots (total ground). Symmetry halves or cancels the signed work, and recognised shapes — triangles, trapezoids, quarter circles — replace anti-derivatives with geometry.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Geometric area = ∫ₐᵇ|f(x)|dx
∫₀ᵃ√(a² − x²)dx = πa²/4; ∫₋ₐᵃf = 2∫₀ᵃf (even), 0 (odd)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Reporting the signed integral as the area when the curve dips below the axis.  ·  Forgetting to split at the roots before integrating.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Reporting the signed integral as the area when the curve dips below the axis.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The dip below*** - a curve crossing the axis mid-interval: the raw integral understates the true area by twice the dipped part - split and add magnitudes.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Find the roots in [a, b] first - they are the split points for geometric area.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Find the area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 3.** — **Sign check:** x² ≥ 0 on [0, 3] ⟹ signed = geometric, no split needed. **Evaluate:** ∫₀³x²dx = [x³/3]₀³ = **9 square units**. **Shape note:** the region is a parabolic segment — no standard shape, so the integral is the tool.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find the geometric area between y = x² − 4 and the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 5.** — **Roots in [0, 5]:** x² − 4 = 0 ⟹ x = 2 (and −2, outside). **Sign strips:** f < 0 on [0, 2) (dips below), f > 0 on (2, 5]. **Piece 1:** ∫₀²(4 − x²)dx = [4x − x³/3]₀² = 8 − 8/3 = 16/3.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One number, two questions: the ledger (net, signed) and the map (total, geometric) - split at roots to convert.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Signed area: above the axis positive, below negative - the integral is a net. Geometric area: integral of |f| - split at the roots, integrate piecewise, add magnitudes. Displacement vs distance is the same distinction. Symmetry: even f halves the work, odd f cancels to zero on [-a, a].…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every integral property has a picture; the picture is the fastest verification.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Evaluate ∫₋₂²x³dx and ∫₋₂²x²dx, and explain the asymmetry.** — **Odd integrand:** x³ is odd ⟹ ∫₋₂²x³dx = **0** — the credit on [0, 2] exactly cancels the debit on [−2, 0]. **Even integrand:** x² is even ⟹ ∫₋₂²x²dx = 2∫₀²x²dx = 2·(8/3) = **16/3**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find the area enclosed by y = √(9 − x²) and the x-axis, and verify by geometry.** — **Recognise the shape:** y² = 9 − x² ⟹ x² + y² = 9 — the upper semicircle of radius 3. **Domain:** −3 ≤ x ≤ 3; the integrand is nonnegative throughout ⟹ no split.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to Area Under a Curve This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to area under a curve: the signed-area reading of the definite integral and the standard area computations in one page.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Signed area:** ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx counts area above the axis positively, below negatively — the integral is a *net*, not a total. - **True (geometric) area:** ∫ₐᵇ|f(x)|dx — split at the axis crossings, integrate each piece, add magnitudes. - **Area between curve and axis:** find the roots of f in [a, b], partition, integrate |f| piecewise.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Signed vs Geometric: The Ledger and the Map - The definite integral is a **ledger** (credits above the axis, debits below — the net displacement reading); the geometric area is a **map** (every region counts positively — the total distance reading).…

Deep Conceptual — Symmetry and Standard Shapes as Shortcuts - **Even/odd symmetry:** for even f, ∫₋ₐᵃf = 2∫₀ᵃf; for odd f, ∫₋ₐᵃf = 0 — the signed ledger cancels symmetric debits and credits. Half the work for even functions, zero work for odd ones.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — simple positive region:** one anti-derivative, endpoints, done. - **Type B — sign change mid-interval:** split at the root, add magnitudes. - **Type C — symmetry shortcut:** even/odd halving or cancellation. - **Type D — recognised shape:** line (triangle) or circle (quarter).  ·  ## 6.
